extracted.intended_audience: EHP authors and contributors, journal editors, and science communicators/journalists
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and criteria for preparing and issuing Environmental Health Perspectives (EHP) press releases that accurately, clearly, and responsibly communicate environmental health research to researchers, practitioners, policy makers, journalists, and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target papers: relevance and importance to audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: EHP issues occasional press releases to publicize papers that we believe are relevant and important to researchers, educators, public health practitioners, policy makers, and/or the general public, as well as to regular EHP readers and contributors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select for publicity those papers likely to benefit one or more of the stated audiences; choices about which papers to publicize influence media coverage, public perception, and possibly policymaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary goal: serve science and the public by increasing awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases should serve science and the public by increasing awareness of work that might otherwise be overlooked by people who would benefit from reading it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor releases that legitimately increase the uptake and understanding of useful research rather than releases produced solely to draw attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure press releases are accurate; avoid presenting misleading or incorrect statements about study findings or implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy includes not overstating results, not inventing causal claims when only associations are shown, and not introducing factual errors that could mislead journalists or the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness: include key information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide key information on current knowledge, research methods, study limitations, and potential conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because many news stories rely heavily on press releases, include sufficient substantive detail (context, methods, limitations, COIs) so that releases do not exaggerate or omit important qualifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity: avoid vague or sensational language
rubrics_metrics.description: Write releases in clear, non-vague language and avoid sensational phrasing that overstates importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow journalistic principles (e.g., Association of Health Care Journalists) to resist vague/sensational words; clarity helps readers and journalists understand the real implications without hype.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualization without inappropriate extrapolation
rubrics_metrics.description: Put findings into context and interpret them without inappropriate extrapolation or exaggeration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how new results fit into existing knowledge and avoid extending conclusions beyond the data (e.g., from animal or observational studies directly to human clinical recommendations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge uncertainty and distinguish association vs causation
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly acknowledge uncertainty in findings and clearly distinguish results that represent associations from those that support causal inferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid implying causation when only associations were observed; state limitations that affect certainty and the need for further research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Report potential conflicts of interest relevant to the research and its interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including COIs in the release helps journalists and readers judge possible biases and improves transparency; omissions can contribute to poor-quality reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible translation/reframing for broad audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Translate and reframe technical findings for a broad audience while maintaining responsibility to improve public understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simplify language and highlight practical implications when appropriate, but do so without sacrificing accuracy, context, or necessary qualifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid exaggeration and sensationalism that undermine credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use attention-getting tactics that sacrifice balance and realistic presentation of implications; exaggeration serves interests but not the public’s interest and can undermine credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize long-term trust and quality of coverage over short-term sensational headlines; sensational press releases may lead to poor-quality health reporting and potential harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide accurate and appropriate information for interviews and media follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: When interacting with journalists (in press releases or interviews), provide accurate and appropriate information to support high-quality science reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to expand on methods, limitations, and implications in interviews; press releases are a key input to journalists and should facilitate, not replace, informed reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial responsibility: be mindful of downstream influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors must recognize that issuing a press release affects which research receives media attention and can shape public opinion and policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that influence responsibly when deciding to publicize studies, balancing potential benefits to public health and scientific discourse against risks of miscommunication.
